summary: Induction on the number m of factors, one tensor factor at a time (map_bilinear), then re-indexing.

steps.lean:
m.rec (single 0 ∘ by simp) fun m i h ↦ ((i (by grind)).map_bilinear (TensorProduct.mk
  ..).flip (h m .refl)).of_eq_isOfFinOrder_smul fun (s, t, u) _ ↦ ⟨1, .one, update (update s _ t) _
  u, by grind [SetLike.mem_coe], congr($(by simp) ⊗ₜ $(TensorChain.pure_congr (by grind)))⟩

steps.claim: m = 0: both sides are the empty pure tensor 1 ∈ ℂ, which is the combination with the single coefficient 1 at the tuple 0 (whose entries lie in the subgroups A_j); d^0 = 1 and |B|^0 = 1.

m → m + 1, with induction hypothesis h for m and the premise i for m + 1. The pure tensor f_m ⊗ (f_{m−1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ f_0) is the image of (f_m, f_{m−1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ f_0) under the bilinear map (a, b) ↦ a ⊗ b; by map_bilinear with the premise for f_m (denominator d, size B) and h (denominator d^m, size |B|^m) it is an admissible combination of the tensors v_m(x) ⊗ (pure tensor of y) over pairs (x, y), with denominator d^{m+1} and size |B|^{m+1}. Each such tensor equals 1·(the pure tensor of the tuple y updated at 2m and 2m + 1 by the two entries of x), whose entries lie in the A_j; so of_eq_isOfFinOrder_smul (ζ = 1) re-indexes the combination by tuples.
